story.title: Kelly Clarkson vs. Art of Play: Footage Revealed of Singer’s Visit to Brooklyn Novelty Store She Slammed for ‘Pretty Woman’ Treatment - Variety

facts.text: Footage of Kelly Clarkson visiting the Brooklyn novelty store she slammed on Saturday has now been acquired and released by Pablo Torre, the host and executive editor of the investigative podcast, “Pablo Torre Finds Out.” The video offers another perspective to the ongoing drama between Clarkson and Art of Play, the Brooklyn local business she …
Huge" shopping scene from Pretty Woman , where Julia Roberts' character is dismissed by store staff based on assumptions about her spending power.
According to the singer, a staff member suggested finding her something "comparable" rather than showing her the products she was interested in.
Clarkson said she felt she was treated as if she could not afford the merchandise and compared the experience to Pretty Woman .
Kelly Clarkson performs during the 2023 Rockefeller Center Christmas tree Lighting Ceremony at Rockefeller Center in New York City on November 29, 2023.
— Kelly Clarkson (@kellyclarkson) October 10, 2026
The store said Clarkson spent about five minutes inside and asked about Molly.
On Saturday, Clarkson posted on X that she had traveled to Brooklyn specifically to visit the store after spotting some "really rad" items she wanted to buy.
Pablo Torre promised us security footage from Kelly Clarkson’s now-viral visit to Art of Play in Brooklyn.
Well, we did get the video on Tuesday night, but no audio — bummer.
We greet everyone who walks in the door with the invitation to ‘pick things up and play.’ And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys.”
For most of her time in the shop, Clarkson can be seen playing around with what appears to be a kaleidoscope near the shop’s entrance.

“Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me,” Miss Independent wrote. “Wow, dude.
Clarkson fans are going to want to look away from a moment like this.
What we could see of the brief visit does not bode well for the “Stronger (What Doesn’t Kill You)” singer.

Footage of Kelly Clarkson visiting the Brooklyn novelty store she slammed on Saturday has now been acquired and released by Pablo Torre, the host and executive editor of the investigative podcast, “Pablo Torre Finds Out.”

After Art of Play shared a statement in response on Sunday, writing that the bird is “permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale” and “plays an important role in the magic shows we host here,” a skeptical Clarkson responded once again , describing the interaction now seen on video and writing: “Cool, cool.

While some are staunchly pro-Clarkson in the debate that has since taken over the internet, others have questioned the singer’s motives for calling out the small business across her social media accounts.

In an interview with Inside Edition on Tuesday, store owner Adam Rubin said that his store has been review-bombed since Clarkson took to social media and named the store, and employees and surrounding businesses have been harassed. “We are afraid for the safety of our shopkeepers.
Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger… Things changed when she used her platform to attack us.
It’s just social warfare,” he said.
Rubin also offered an explanation for why Clarkson might have felt she received subpar treatment: “When Kelly came in, the shop was crowded.
We treated her like a normal person, but apparently that did not live up to her expectations.”
At this point in the footage, Clarkson and the employee part ways as he begins helping other customers in the store.

From footage from an alternative camera angle, we can see Clarkson then find herself standing in front of the automaton bird, where she then gets the attention of a store employee, who can be seen speaking with the musician and pointing at something by the bird, though it is not clear from the video what he was pointing at.
